idiom_name: SQLAlchemy relationship cascade 'all, delete-orphan' with Session flush
implementation_notes: SQLAlchemy expresses the composite in the mapper: the root owns its dependents through relationship(...) with cascade='all, delete-orphan', the Session is the unit of work, and one flush writes the root and every dependent change together. delete-orphan is the load-bearing half - it deletes a dependent the moment it is de-associated, which is exactly the child lifecycle the classic pattern demanded, while plain save-update only registers children in the same session.
code_sketch:
class Order(Base):
    __tablename__ = "orders"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    lines: Mapped[list[OrderLine]] = relationship(
        back_populates="order", cascade="all, delete-orphan")

with Session(engine) as s:          # unit of work
    o = s.get(Order, oid)
    o.lines.pop()                   # orphan -> DELETE
    s.commit()                      # root + children flushed once
pitfalls: 'all' implies refresh-expire, which expires children aggressively and is documented as unsuitable under the asyncio extension; prefer an explicit cascade list there.
In a bi-directional pair only the parent side cascades save-update: assigning child.order = parent does not place the child in the session.
delete-orphan requires a single-parent relationship; sharing the same dependent between two parents raises instead of persisting.

variants.name: Django inline formsets and admin inlines
variants.implementation_notes: Django has no graph-tracking mapper, so the composite is assembled by hand: a ModelForm plus an inline formset validates parent and dependent rows together and writes them in one transaction, and ModelAdmin inlines give the same unit in the admin. The dependent models still carry their own ForeignKey, so this realizes Composite Entity at the interaction layer - the coarse-grained object the caller saves - rather than in the persistence mapping; choose it when Django is already the stack and the cluster is always edited as a whole.
pitfalls: The ORM does not enforce the cluster boundary: a stray OrderLine.objects.create() writes a row the coarse-grained object will later overwrite.
inlineformset_factory drops rows unless can_delete and extra are set deliberately, so deletions look implemented but are never persisted.
